paper_title: Dithiene-fused quinoxalineimide-based all-acceptor polymers for n-type organic semiconductors

knowledge_points.content: Dithiene-fused quinoxalineimide (DTQI) is a novel strong electron-deficient building block that combines the structural features of bithiophene imide (BTI) and quinoxaline (Qx).
knowledge_points.evidence: In this work, a strong electron-deficient building block, dithiene-fused quinoxalineimide (DTQI), containing electron-withdrawing quinoxaline and imide units, was synthesized and incorporated into a polymer backbone... Fig. 1 Molecular design strategy to develop electron-deficient building block DTQI, which combines the advantages of both BTI and Qx.

knowledge_points.content: The all-acceptor (A–A) type polymers PDTQI and P(DTQI-BTI) were synthesized via Stille coupling polymerization using Pd2(dba)3/P(o-tol)3 as the catalyst system.
knowledge_points.evidence: The polymerization of DTQI-2Br was carried out with comonomers bis(tributyltin) and distannylated BTI (BTI-Tin) via the Stille coupling reaction using Pd2(dba)3/P(o-tol)3 as the catalyst system to afford A–A type polymers PDTQI and P(DTQI-BTI)

knowledge_points.content: The copolymer P(DTQI-BTI) exhibits a unipolar n-type electron mobility (μe) of 0.25 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ in organic thin-film transistors.
knowledge_points.evidence: P(DTQI-BTI) showed a high μe of >0.25 cm2 V−1 s−1... while the copolymer P(DTQI-BTI) showed unipolar n-type charge transport and exhibited one order higher electron mobility of 0.25 cm2 V−1 s−1 than PDTQI.

knowledge_points.content: The homopolymer PDTQI exhibits ambipolar charge transport with a hole mobility (μh) of 0.005 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ and an electron mobility (μe) of 0.012 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹.
knowledge_points.evidence: The homopolymer PDTQI exhibits ambipolar charge transport in OTFT. The PDTQI-based device showed μh and μe of 0.005 and 0.012 cm2 V−1 s−1, respectively

knowledge_points.content: The incorporation of the dithiene-fused quinoxalineimide (DTQI) unit results in deep-lying LUMO energy levels (<-3.50 eV), which facilitates electron injection and suppresses hole accumulation.
knowledge_points.evidence: Due to the strong electron-withdrawing ability of the imide and quinoxaline groups, DTQI has significantly enhanced electron-deficient characteristics... DTQI-based acceptor–acceptor type polymers PDTQI and P(DTQI-BTI) showed deep FMO energy levels, which is beneficial for electron transport in OTFTs.

knowledge_points.content: P(DTQI-BTI) thin films demonstrate higher crystallinity and stronger molecular aggregation compared to PDTQI, as evidenced by a higher root-mean-square (RMS) roughness of 0.515 nm versus 0.408 nm.
knowledge_points.evidence: For P(DTQI-BTI), its surfaces are rougher with higher RMS values of 0.515 nm, indicating higher crystallinity... the higher electron mobility of P(DTQI-BTI) might be due to its stronger aggregation of molecules to form films with higher crystallinity.

knowledge_points.content: The OTFT devices were fabricated using a top-gate/bottom-contact (TGBC) structure with Ag gate electrodes and polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) as the dielectric layer.
knowledge_points.evidence: OTFTs with a top-gate/bottom contact (TGBC) device structure were fabricated. Polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) is used as the dielectric and Ag is used as the gate electrode.

knowledge_points.content: DFT calculations show that the DTQI monomer possesses a completely planar structure with a calculated LUMO level of -2.60 eV, which is 0.3 eV lower than that of the BTI building block.
knowledge_points.evidence: The optimized molecular geometry of DTQI is a completely planar structure (Fig. S10, ESI†)... The LUMO level of the DTQI is 0.3 eV lower than the calculated LUMO level of the BTI.

knowledge_points.content: Optimal OTFT performance for DTQI-based polymers was achieved by processing from chloroform solution at 5 mg/mL followed by thermal annealing at 100 °C for 20 minutes.
knowledge_points.evidence: Chloroform is chosen as the processing solvent and the concentration of organic semiconductors is controlled at 5 mg mL−1. Before evaluation, an annealing process at 100 °C for 20 min was conducted to achieve better morphology.

knowledge_points.content: Both PDTQI and P(DTQI-BTI) polymers exhibit high thermal stability with 5% weight loss decomposition temperatures exceeding 400 °C.
knowledge_points.evidence: As shown in Fig. S9 (ESI†), both polymers exhibited excellent thermal stability with the decomposition temperature (5% weight loss) over 400 °C.

knowledge_points.content: The optical band gaps (Eg^opt) for both PDTQI and P(DTQI-BTI) were determined to be 1.98 eV, based on the absorption onsets of the polymer films.
knowledge_points.evidence: The optical band gaps (Eg^opt s) of PDTQI and P(DTQI-BTI) are 1.98 eV, determined from the polymer film absorption onsets.

knowledge_points.content: P(DTQI-BTI) achieves an on/off current ratio (Ion/Ioff) of approximately 10^5 and a threshold voltage (Vth) of approximately 10 V in OTFT devices.
knowledge_points.evidence: Besides, a high on/off current (Ion/Ioff) ratio of around 10^5 and a relatively low threshold voltage (Vth) of 10 V are also achieved by P(DTQI-BTI).
